title: Log Sentinel
one_liner: Every line of a synthetic seven-service log firehose is judged in real time (actionable, severity, category, security) and scored live against a regex/severity-level alerting baseline with hand-labelled ground truth.
platform: web (vite/react) with a Node SSE stream server; the Node server holds the API key and runs the whole pipeline
what_it_does: The page is a three-pane dark ops console. The left pane is a firehose of raw log lines from seven services (api-gateway JSON, payments JSON plus Java stack traces, auth logfmt, k8s events, postgres, nginx access logs, cron) replayed from a seeded deterministic generator at 1-400 lines/s (slider, default 40). Multi-line stack traces are grouped into one event in code. Each event is sent to Jev with four questions (actionable, severity 0-4, category, security). When the verdict returns, the line gets a severity color and an age badge (ms from emission to verdict). The middle pane groups actionable events into incident cards by service:category inside a 60 s window (in code), with first/last seen, count, max severity and a security pill. The right pane shows live metrics (events/s, judgments/s, in-flight, backlog, p50/p95/p99, errors), a batching calibration result (single vs batch x8, measured at startup), and a "Regex rules vs Jev" scoreboard with precision/recall computed continuously against the fixture ground truth, plus a list of regex mistakes (false pages and misses) and any Jev mistakes. A Storm button injects a 14-step payments-provider degradation that starts with INFO-level anomalies and only produces ERRORs after 5.4 s; a storm timeline shows when Jev first flagged it versus when regex first paged, and prints the lead in seconds. Controls: rate slider, concurrency slider, batch/single toggle, pause. MOCK=1 replays fixture labels without calling the API.

jev_questions.instructions: Should an on-call engineer look at the log line `events[i].line` (emitted by the service `events[i].service`) right now? Judge what the line means for the system, NOT its log level or the words it contains. A failed attempt that recovered, an expected or canary failure, a client hanging up (HTTP 499, context canceled), a single wrong password, a diagnostic dump, an idempotent duplicate-key retry, a 404 or a deprecation notice is NOT actionable even if it says ERROR or contains a stack trace. A line that looks successful but reveals silent failure (HTTP 200 with a 0-byte body on a checkout or payment path, backup wrote 0 bytes, reconciliation mismatch), a request that took many seconds (rt/urt of several seconds), capacity running out, replication lag, a certificate about to expire, a dangerous privilege grant or scale-down, credential stuffing or vulnerability scanning IS actionable even at INFO level or with a 2xx status. | true: A human should investigate now: the line indicates customer impact, silent failure, data loss or risk, capacity exhaustion, a dangerous change, or a security event. | false: Routine, expected, self-healed, or merely informational. Nobody needs to act on this line.
jev_questions.state_shape: batch: {events:[{service,line}]} with keys e{i}_actionable/e{i}_severity/e{i}_category/e{i}_security, 5-16 events per request (default 8); single: {event:{service,line}} with unprefixed keys. Threshold: actionable if P >= 0.5.

jev_questions.instructions: How severe is the situation described by the log line `events[i].line` for the production system? Judge the consequence, not the log level: a successful retry or an expected canary failure is noise even if it says ERROR; a silent failure (backup wrote 0 bytes, HTTP 200 with an empty body on a payment path, reconciliation mismatch, replication lag, cert expiring) is at least degraded even at INFO; a routine autoscaler or deploy event with no failure is at most degraded.
options: 0 Noise: routine, expected, or already self-healed. Nothing is wrong.
1 Informational: worth knowing (a deprecation notice, a blocked scan, a one-off client error) but there is no service impact.
2 Degraded: performance, capacity, freshness or reliability is slipping, or a risky change was made. Customers are not failing yet.
3 Customer-impacting: some customers are failing, waiting far too long, or getting wrong or unknown results right now.
4 Outage: the service or a core dependency is down, or effectively every request is failing.
jev_questions.state_shape: same batch state; score 0-4 rounded to SEVERITIES index [noise, informational, degraded, customer-impacting, outage]

jev_questions.instructions: What is the root-cause category of the log line `events[i].line`?
options: deploy: A rollout, new image, or version change caused it.
capacity: A resource is running out or overloaded: memory, disk, connections, replicas, queue depth, replication lag, latency under load.
dependency_failure: An upstream provider or another service is failing, timing out, or returning bad or empty responses.
security: Authentication, authorization, privilege grants, scanning, credential stuffing or other abuse.
data_integrity: Data is missing, mismatched, unreconciled, stale, or a backup wrote nothing.
config: A configuration value, certificate, feature flag or scaling setting is wrong, dangerous or about to expire.
transient: A one-off blip that already recovered on its own (a retry that succeeded, a client that hung up).
noise: Normal operation. Nothing is wrong.
jev_questions.state_shape: same batch state; answer.choice must be one of CATEGORIES, else falls back to noise; answer.confidence shown as categoryConfidence

jev_questions.instructions: Is the log line `events[i].line` security-relevant: credential attacks, vulnerability scanning or probing, privilege or scope grants, suspicious tokens, or abuse? | true: The line describes or strongly suggests a security event that a security or on-call engineer should know about. | false: Not a security matter (ordinary logins, refreshes, blocked rate limits and normal traffic are not security events).

request_cadence: Continuous stream. Default 40 lines/s, batched 8 events per request with a 40 ms linger, concurrency 8, so about 5 requests/s at default and up to ~25 requests/s at 200 lines/s. Each request carries 4 questions per event (32 answers per batch of 8). Startup calibration fires 16 single + 2 batch requests. Storm injects 14 events over 7.8 s on top of the stream. 429s trigger shared exponential backoff 250 ms -> 8 s and one requeue.

dm1_mapping.dm1_body: POST /yes-no {"texts": ["[payments] {\"ts\":...,\"level\":\"ERROR\",\"msg\":\"charge attempt 1 failed: provider timeout; retry succeeded on attempt 2\",...}", ... up to 32 lines, each prefixed "[<service>] "], "statement": "An on-call engineer should investigate this log line right now.", "when_true": "The line shows customer impact, a silent failure (HTTP 200 with a 0-byte body on a payment or checkout path, a backup that wrote 0 bytes, a reconciliation mismatch), a request that took many seconds, capacity running out, replication lag, a certificate about to expire, a dangerous privilege grant or scale-down, credential stuffing or vulnerability scanning, even at INFO level or with a 2xx status.", "when_false": "The line is routine, expected, or already self-healed: a retry that succeeded, a client that hung up (HTTP 499, context canceled), a single wrong password, a canary failure, a diagnostic thread dump, a duplicate-key retry, a 404, a deprecation notice, or a startup probe, even if it says ERROR or contains a stack trace."} -> results[i].answer / results[i].probability; actionable = probability >= 0.5 (keep ACTIONABLE_THRESHOLD).
dm1_mapping.notes: Service name goes into the text prefix because there is no separate state field. Multi-line stack traces are sent joined with \n as one text; consider truncating traces to the head plus first 2 frames to save tokens.

A successful retry, an expected canary failure or a client hang-up is noise even if it says ERROR.", "Informational: worth knowing (a deprecation notice, a blocked scan, a one-off client error) but there is no service impact.", "Degraded: performance, capacity, freshness or reliability is slipping, or a risky change was made. Customers are not failing yet. A silent failure at INFO level (backup wrote 0 bytes, replication lag, cert expiring) is at least degraded.", "Customer-impacting: some customers are failing, waiting far too long, or getting wrong or unknown results right now (HTTP 200 with an empty body on a payment path, reconciliation mismatch, 5xx on checkout).", "Outage: the service or a core dependency is down, or effectively every request is failing."]} -> results[i].level is the SEVERITIES index; severityScore = results[i].score * 4.
dm1_mapping.notes: Jev's question prose is folded into the level descriptions since /rate has no instruction field.

POST /yes-no {"texts": [same 32 prefixed lines], "statement": "This log line describes a security event.", "when_true": "Credential attacks or credential stuffing, vulnerability scanning or probing, an admin or wildcard privilege or scope grant, a suspicious token, or abuse.", "when_false": "Ordinary logins, token refreshes, a single wrong password, a blocked rate limit, or normal traffic."} -> security = probability >= 0.5.
dm1_mapping.notes: Optional fourth request. To save a request per batch derive security = (category === "security"); fixture truth agrees with this for every template. Ship derived first, add the yes-no call only if the scoreboard shows security misses.

browser_plan: Move the whole pipeline into the browser as a React island; the only server piece is a thin proxy route (/api/dm1/:route) that adds the bearer key and forwards JSON to https://api.milliseconds.ai/v1/decision-machine-1/:route, passing back status, body, x-inference-ms and x-input-tokens. Copy fixtures/generator/grouper/regex/incidents/metrics/rng/types unchanged (all pure TS). Replace server/jev.ts with a browser judge(events) that sends the same batch of up to 32 prefixed lines to /yes-no (actionable), /rate (severity) and /classify (category) in parallel via the proxy, then zips results into Verdict[] (security derived from category, or a fourth /yes-no call). Rewrite pipeline.ts as a client-side scheduler: a setInterval generator tick at the chosen rate, a 300 ms linger that fills batches up to 32, a token bucket of 2 requests/s (one batch = 3 requests, so about 0.67 batches/s, ~21 events/s ceiling), max 2 batches in flight, and 429 handling that honours Retry-After, backs off 1 s -> 16 s, pauses the generator (not just the judge) so the backlog stays honest, shows a "rate limited, shared demo key" banner, and requeues the batch once. Delete the startup calibration and the batch/single toggle and concurrency slider; the Batching panel becomes a static explainer: "32 lines x 3 routes per batch, 2 req/s budget" with live x-inference-ms and x-input-tokens totals. Rate slider 1-20 lines/s, default 12. Keep the store reducer and all three panes; replace EventSource with direct dispatch. Keep the Storm button and timeline (first flag by decision-machine vs first regex page). Keep MOCK as a query flag (?mock=1) so the page still renders if the key is rotated. Style with the milliseconds site tokens instead of the Jev dark palette; keep severity colors as CSS variables. Show precision/recall honestly; do not hardcode the README numbers.
risks: Ambiguous whether texts[] and statements[] combine in one /yes-no call; the plan assumes texts + a single statement per request. If they do combine, actionable + security fit in one request.

Rate budget: 3 requests per batch at 2 req/s caps sustained throughput near 21 lines/s, far below the original 40-150 lines/s story; the demo must frame the ceiling as the shared demo key, not the API. Multiple concurrent visitors share the org's 200 req/min, so one tab at full rate can starve others; add a per-tab cap (12 lines/s default) and keep the 429 banner clear.
Latency of a 32-text batch is unknown; if p50 is 500 ms or more, the firehose age badges will read 400-900 ms instead of ~200 ms. Show it, do not hide it.

Accuracy will not match the README's 100/100 claims: 8-way classify on terse JSON/logfmt lines may pick neighbours (capacity vs config on scale-down), and /rate with 5 verbose levels may land one level off. Incident grouping is by category, so category flips split incidents.
Multi-line Java stack traces (5-6 lines) cost 150-250 input tokens each across 3 routes; at 20 lines/s that is fine for the 1M tok/min budget but truncation to head + 2 frames is cheap insurance.

Storm timing: linger (300 ms) plus batch latency delays the first decision-machine flag; the lead over regex (first page at +5.4 s) should still be 4 s or more, but measure it before quoting a number.

The original Node server ran generator timing with setInterval at 20 ms; in a background browser tab timers throttle to 1 s, so the stream stalls when the tab is hidden. Pause on visibilitychange and say so.
The two screenshot assets are not usable (6.9 MB webp); take new screenshots after restyling.
